votes.plain_language: The House voted to accept the Senate's rewrite of H.R. 5334, which imposes Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, extends an Iran sanctions law, and also expands a teacher tax deduction to early-childhood educators. A Yea accepts that Senate version. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors.

The national average gas price has exceeded $4 per gallon on 158 days this year, setting a new record for the most days above $4 in a single year.

For families across South Texas, these costs add up quickly. Whether it is driving to work, taking children to school, or running a small business, higher fuel prices are taking more money out of household budgets. Truck drivers, farmers, and ranchers are also paying more to operate, which can lead to higher prices for the goods and services families depend on every day.

According to Moody’s Analytics chief economist Mark Zandi, the war in Iran has cost the average American household nearly $2,000 through higher energy prices, borrowing costs, and military spending. That is a significant financial burden at a time when families are already dealing with higher costs for groceries, housing, and other everyday necessities.

Congress needs to take the economic consequences of this war seriously. Families across South Texas are already paying more at the pump and for everyday necessities. We need to focus on lowering energy costs and providing relief to the families and businesses dealing with these higher prices.

Families across Starr County depend on reliable water service, and communities like Roma and Escobares have dealt with flooding for years.

In the House-passed Water Resources Development Act of 2026, I secured a $7.5 million authorization for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to support water and wastewater infrastructure improvements in Starr County, including improvements to water supply and distribution systems.

The bill also authorizes the Army Corps to study flood risks in Roma and Escobares and identify potential solutions to reduce flooding. These studies are an important first step toward protecting homes, roads, and businesses from future flood damage.

I will continue working to get these provisions through final passage and secure the federal funding needed to improve water infrastructure and address flooding in Starr County.

Last Friday, my Outreach Coordinator, Kassandra Herrera, attended the Business Expo Laredo 2026 Press Conference and Exhibitors’ VIP Dinner at the Falcon Bank Event Center.

This event provided an opportunity to engage with local business owners, exhibitors, and community members and celebrate their contributions to Laredo’s business community.

It was a pleasure connecting with Chief Tim Tubbs, Priscilla Pantoja Johnson, Director of the Laredo Motor Carriers Association, Mr. Sanchez from the Mexican Consulate, and local business owner, Gloria from Cakes of Glory along with attendees.

My office is grateful for opportunities like these that foster connections, strengthen community partnerships, and celebrate the spirit of local business in Laredo.

Families in Jim Hogg County depend on reliable water infrastructure for their homes, businesses, and everyday needs.

In the House-passed Water Resources Development Act of 2026, I secured a $7.5 million authorization for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to support water infrastructure improvements in Jim Hogg County.

This authorization could help replace aging water lines, reduce water loss, and improve the reliability of the county’s water distribution system. These improvements are important for ensuring residents have access to safe, dependable drinking water.

This is an important step for Jim Hogg County, but we still need to secure the funding to make these improvements a reality. I will continue working to get this legislation through final passage and bring federal water infrastructure investments back to South Texas.

Today, I was pleased to announce $210,000 in federal funding through the U.S. Economic Development Administration’s Partnership Planning Program to support the South Texas Development Council’s regional economic development efforts in Webb, Zapata, Jim Hogg and Starr counties.

This funding will help STDC update and implement the region’s Comprehensive Economic Development Strategy - a roadmap for supporting job creation, workforce development, infrastructure improvements and business growth.

It will also support planning and technical assistance for local communities, helping leaders coordinate development projects and pursue additional resources. This assistance is especially valuable for rural communities with limited planning resources.

Congratulations and thank you to Juan Rodriguez and the STDC team for your continued dedication to South Texas! I’ll continue working to bring federal resources home to help our communities grow and expand opportunities for residents across our region.

Last night, I was pleased to join @LULAC Council #12 for the 2026 Tejano Achievers Awards Dinner, celebrating ten outstanding community leaders and professionals whose accomplishments and service have made a meaningful difference in Laredo.

I also had the honor of presenting Congressional Recognitions to these community leaders in appreciation of their professional achievements, leadership and dedication to serving others.

Congratulations to all of this year’s Tejano Achievers! Thank you to LULAC Council #12 for recognizing the individuals who continue to strengthen Laredo and South Texas.

Today, I was proud to announce $938,000 in federal Community Project Funding for renovations to the Hebbronville Community Center. I secured this funding through the FY2027 appropriations process, and it is included in the appropriations bill.

The Community Center is an important gathering place for Jim Hogg County residents, hosting public events, community meetings, and the County Fair. These funds would support a new roof, structural improvements, an upgraded HVAC system, a commercial kitchen, and essential plumbing, electrical, and restroom upgrades. The improvements would also strengthen the facility’s ability to serve as an emergency shelter during hurricanes, flooding, and other disasters.

This investment builds on the $1.285 million secured for Kohler Park improvements and $1 million for the Jim Hogg County Emergency Response Center. Together, these projects support community recreation, public safety, and emergency preparedness throughout the county.

Today, I was proud to announce the Community Water and Energy Resource Center (CWERC) Feasibility Study, an important initiative that will explore innovative solutions to strengthen Laredo’s water supply, improve wastewater treatment, and expand renewable energy opportunities.

The proposed facility would reclaim and reuse wastewater, transform organic waste into renewable energy, and help create a more sustainable and locally controlled water resource for our community. If determined feasible, the facility could potentially recycle 2 to 3 million gallons of wastewater per day, helping reduce our dependence on the Rio Grande while meeting Laredo’s growing water needs.

This initiative is supported by $180,000 in federal funding from the North American Development Bank’s Technical Assistance Program, along with $81,500 in additional funding from RGISC, the City of Laredo, Harvard Graduate School of Design, and Zimmerman Consulting, bringing the total project investment to $261,500.

Beyond strengthening our water supply, this project could create economic opportunities, support local job creation, provide reclaimed water for businesses and irrigation, and recover valuable resources from waste. The feasibility study will evaluate the project’s engineering, environmental benefits, potential locations, and economic viability to help determine the best path forward.

I look forward to continuing our partnership with NADBank, RGISC, the City of Laredo, and our other partners to advance innovative solutions that protect our natural resources, strengthen our long-term water security, and support Laredo’s continued growth. Planning for our future means investing in sustainable solutions that will benefit our community for generations to come.

Laredo is growing, and our water and wastewater infrastructure needs to keep up with the needs of our community.

In the House-passed Water Resources Development Act of 2026, I secured a $25 million authorization for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to support water and wastewater infrastructure improvements in Laredo.

This authorization could help replace aging water lines, reduce water loss, strengthen our water supply, and improve drainage in neighborhoods that experience repeated flooding. It could also support environmental restoration projects that help protect our waterways and reduce flood risks.

This is an important step toward improving Laredo’s water infrastructure, but there is still work to be done. I will continue working to get this legislation across the finish line and secure the federal funding needed to move these projects forward.

Small businesses across South Texas are dealing with higher costs and growing uncertainty, making it harder for owners to pay their employees, invest in their businesses, and plan for the future.

A new survey of 1,171 small business owners by Small Business for America’s Future found that 64% have cut or skipped their own pay to keep their businesses running. Many are also delaying investments because of uncertainty surrounding federal economic policies.

For small businesses in South Texas, tariffs and rising operating costs affect everything from purchasing supplies to hiring workers. These businesses support local jobs, provide important services, and contribute to our communities.

I will continue working across the aisle to lower costs, support predictable trade policies, and make sure our small businesses have the opportunity to compete and grow.

My office recently recognized Andrea Ortega for her work serving the people of Texas’s 28th Congressional District as an intern in our San Antonio office.

Originally from Mexico City, Andrea is a senior at the University of Texas at San Antonio, where she is majoring in marketing. After graduation, she hopes to pursue a career in corporate marketing.

Thank you, Andrea, for your hard work and dedication to our constituents. We appreciate having you as part of our team, and I wish you all the best as you finish your studies and pursue your career goals. Congratulations!

My office recently helped deliver a book donation from the Library of Congress to the Pleasanton Public Library!

Outreach Coordinator Kelly Brooks joined Library Director Gina Steward to celebrate the donation and help provide more reading and educational materials for the community.

Local libraries play an important role in helping students learn, encouraging children to read, and providing families with access to books and other resources.

Thank you to Gina and the Pleasanton Public Library staff for the work they do to support literacy and education in Atascosa County. I will continue working to connect our local libraries with federal resources that benefit our communities.

Inflation moved in the wrong direction in September. Consumer prices rose 3.7% over the past year, up from 3.4% in August, while gasoline prices jumped 9.1% in just one month.

For families across South Texas, higher fuel prices mean more than paying extra at the pump. Truck drivers, farmers, ranchers, and small businesses are also dealing with higher operating costs, which can lead to higher prices for the goods and services families depend on every day.

Families are already stretching their paychecks to cover groceries, housing, utilities, and health care. Congress needs to focus on bringing these costs down and providing relief to working families and small businesses.

I will continue working with Republicans and Democrats to address rising costs, support South Texas workers and businesses, and help families keep more of their hard-earned money.

Behind every grant is a student working toward a brighter future. 

As an author of the TEXAS Grant Program during my time in the Texas Legislature, I’m proud to see its lasting impact.

Hear from Dahlia Vasquez and Silvia Silva about how TEXAS and Pell Grants have supported their college journeys at TAMIU and Laredo College.

I’ll continue working to make higher education more affordable for South Texas families.

For many families in South Texas, school breakfast and lunch programs help make sure their children have nutritious meals while easing the cost of groceries at home.

In the FY27 House Agriculture Appropriations bill, I helped secure $37.9 billion for Child Nutrition programs, including the National School Lunch Program, School Breakfast Program, and Summer Food Programs.

These programs help provide students with healthy meals throughout the school year and during the summer months when school is out. They also provide important support for working parents and families who are already dealing with high food costs.

Children should be able to focus on learning, not worrying about their next meal. As a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, I will continue working to protect these programs and make sure South Texas families have access to the resources they depend on.

My office recently joined Yuliana Guerra to celebrate the grand opening of Baglory, a new café cart located inside her mother Gloria Guerra’s bakery, Cakes of Glory, in Laredo!

It is great to see this mother-daughter team working together to grow their businesses. Small businesses are an important part of Laredo’s economy, and it is always good to see local entrepreneurs investing in our community.

Congratulations to Yuliana and Gloria on this milestone! I wish them both continued success and encourage the Laredo community to stop by and support these local businesses.

More Texans will now have access to federal Pell Grants to help pay for short-term job training programs.

Five Texas community colleges have been approved to offer eligible Workforce Pell programs, including Texas Southmost College in Brownsville. These programs will help students train for careers in fields like welding, health care, HVAC, and machining.

I supported expanding Pell Grant eligibility to include short-term trade and workforce training programs because students should have access to federal financial assistance whether they are pursuing a college degree or learning a skilled trade. This change will help more Texans gain the skills they need for good-paying jobs.

I encourage eligible Texans to explore these opportunities by completing the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at https://t.co/8wv08KYFRt and contacting a participating college to learn more.

I also encourage other colleges across South Texas to seek approval for their workforce training programs so more students in our region can benefit from this federal assistance. Expanding access to affordable education and job training is important for our students, workers, and local economy.

The cost of living remains a major concern for families across South Texas. Groceries, housing, utilities, and health care continue to take a large share of household budgets, and many Americans are worried about their financial future.

A new poll found that nearly four in ten Americans believe they would be worse off financially if Republicans maintain control of Congress. These concerns should be taken seriously. Families want to know they can afford their everyday expenses and have some financial security.

Congress needs to focus on lowering costs, protecting Medicare and Social Security, and supporting good-paying jobs. Families who work hard every day should not have to worry about whether their paycheck will cover their basic needs.

I will continue working across the aisle to address the cost of living, support our small businesses, and make sure the needs of South Texas families are heard in Washington.

post.text:
The House passed the bipartisan Major Richard Star Act (H.R. 2102) yesterday morning, which I supported to end the “wounded veteran tax.”

Combat-injured veterans who were forced to medically retire should not have to choose between their military retirement pay and VA disability compensation. This bill would allow eligible veterans to receive both benefits in full.

Our veterans have earned these benefits through their service and sacrifice. I urge the Senate to pass this legislation so we can get it signed into law.
